solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pakistani city’s expression of pleasure in folk wisdom (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the pleasurable AH is set inside the LORE

annotation.surface: Someone praising a city's delight in its traditional sayings.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay, not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lahore, capital of Punjab province, is Pakistan's second-largest city.

entries.clue: Malt vinegar porter possibly put on fish (6)

indicatorNotes.put on: in a down clue, ALE is placed on top of GAR

blocks.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
the gar is a long-snouted fish

annotation.surface: A recipe note: malt vinegar and porter sprinkled over fish, chip-shop style.
annotation.walkthrough: Alegar is literally 'ale-eager', sour ale, as vinegar is sour wine; 'possibly' flags porter as one example of ale.
annotation.definitionFit: Alegar is the old word for vinegar made from malt or ale.

entries.clue: Let former pupils time violent disturbance (11)

blocks.note: a ruction is a noisy row

annotation.surface: An instruction to allow the old boys their moment of rowdiness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like a verb meaning allow; here it is the noun, as in 'without let or hindrance'. Old boys are former pupils of a British school.
annotation.definitionFit: A let is an obstruction or hindrance, the sense kept in legal phrasing and in tennis.

entries.clue: Company is breaking record in this place where all life exists (9)

indicatorNotes.breaking: CO'S breaks into EP, splitting it

annotation.surface: A firm disrupting a record at a venue that apparently contains all living things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company is' shrinks to CO'S, the way 'the company's here' contracts in speech.
annotation.definitionFit: The ecosphere is the part of a planet, or the universe, where life can exist.

entries.clue: Exercises old Turkish ruler before a horsey event (8)

indicatorNotes.before: GYM and KHAN come before A

blocks.note: gym = physical exercises, as in school gym
khan was a title of Turkish and Mongol rulers

annotation.surface: A sultan warming up before a riding competition.
annotation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a British children's pony show with races and games.
annotation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is an event of horse-riding competitions.

entries.clue: Information exists on cover of economics book (7)

indicatorNotes.on: 'on' in the sense of 'added on to', so IS is tacked onto the end of ES
indicatorNotes.cover of: the outside letters of economics, E and S

annotation.surface: A remark that the facts are printed on the jacket of an economics textbook.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen, as in 'get the gen', is British slang for information. 'Book' looks like part of 'economics book'; it is the definition, a book of the Bible.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Genesis opens the Old Testament, one book among the Bible's many.

entries.clue: Former of rock group’s first to be introduced to mother (5)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of group
indicatorNotes.to be introduced to: to introduce something is to bring it in, so G is brought into the middle of MAMA

annotation.surface: A former member of a rock band being presented to someone's mum.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'former of rock group' to be an ex-band member; 'former' is really 'something that forms', and the definition stops at 'rock'.
annotation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock that cools to form igneous rock.

entries.clue: It may carry bricks intended ultimately to shore up house (3)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of intended
indicatorNotes.to shore up: in a down clue, D sits beneath HO, propping it up

annotation.surface: A builder's load of bricks meant to prop up a house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shore up' is building language in the surface; here it places D underneath HO.
annotation.definitionFit: A hod is the open trough on a pole that labourers use to carry bricks.

entries.clue: Film last of participants in modern dance? (8)

indicatorNotes.last of: take the final letter of participants
indicatorNotes.in: S goes in between NEW and REEL

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

annotation.surface: A question about filming the final dancers in a contemporary dance piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Modern dance' reads as one art form, but the two words work separately, with the S slotted between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A newsreel is a short film of current events once shown in cinemas.

entries.clue: Stirrer’s offspring crossing river after meal (8)

indicatorNotes.crossing: SON goes across PO, holding it

blocks.note: tea = an evening meal in Britain
the Po is Italy's longest river

annotation.surface: A troublemaker's child wading across a river after dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stirrer' suggests a troublemaker; it is literal, a thing that stirs, and the ’s means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is what you stir your tea with.

entries.clue: Wearing formal dress, visit Asian warehouse (6)

indicatorNotes.Wearing: DO is dressed in GOWN, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to do a place is to visit it, as in 'do Paris'

annotation.surface: Dressing up smartly to call at a warehouse in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is one word, not 'go down'.
annotation.definitionFit: A godown is a warehouse in India and East Asia, from Malay gudang.

entries.clue: Persian governor beginning to swig a gin? (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of swig

blocks.note: a gin is a snare or trap

annotation.surface: An ancient governor starting to knock back a gin.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'gin' is not the drink but the trap, as in gin trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

entries.clue: Small daughter embracing pale woman’s bird minder (8)

indicatorNotes.embracing: S and D hug WAN and HER between them

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
a woman's thing is her thing

annotation.surface: A little girl hugging a pale woman who looks after birds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman’s' supplies the possessive HER, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A swanherd is someone who tends swans.

entries.clue: Unusually lucky, he’s accommodating single shrub (11)

indicatorNotes.Unusually: the letters of LUCKY HE'S are rearranged
indicatorNotes.accommodating: the rearranged letters take ONE inside

annotation.surface: A man with remarkable luck putting up a lone bush.
annotation.walkthrough: ONE slots in after the H of the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Honeysuckle is a climbing shrub with fragrant flowers.

entries.clue: Engineering con, he emerges as dealer in Cheshire? (12)

indicatorNotes.Engineering: the letters are engineered, built into a new order

annotation.surface: A swindler turning up as a trader somewhere in Cheshire.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county, and also the crumbly cheese named after it; the question mark marks the cheese, a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A cheesemonger sells cheese, Cheshire among them.

entries.clue: Shabby trick binding husband in the interim (9)

indicatorNotes.binding: WILE ties H up inside itself

blocks.note: mean = shabby, as in a mean street

annotation.surface: A low ruse involving tying up a husband for the time being.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shabby trick' reads as one noun phrase, but each word gives its own piece, and the husband is tied inside the second.
annotation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the intervening time.

entries.clue: Marine creature regularly seen swimming ashore? (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter of seen
indicatorNotes.swimming: the letters of ashore move about

annotation.surface: A sea animal spotted swimming towards the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: a seahorse swimming ashore would indeed be a horse on land.
annotation.definitionFit: The seahorse is a small upright marine fish.

entries.clue: Big house rebuilt pine shelter by Iowa railway? (12)

indicatorNotes.rebuilt: the letters of PINE are reassembled
indicatorNotes.by: the pieces sit next to each other

annotation.surface: A mansion reconstructed from pinewood next to a Midwestern railway line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big house' suggests a mansion; it is American slang for a prison, fitting the Iowa setting.
annotation.definitionFit: A penitentiary is a prison, called the big house in US slang.

entries.clue: Ball fits in tiny piece of furniture (7)

indicatorNotes.fits: BALL in fits, convulsed into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside TOY

blocks.note: a toy dog is a tiny breed

annotation.surface: A ball squeezing into a very small piece of furniture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fits in' looks like a single insertion phrase; 'fits' is the anagram signal and 'in' the insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, a British term.

entries.clue: Fish had to form mental images (6)

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: Someone forced to picture fish in their mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had to' reads as obligation; 'had' is ATE and 'to' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from psychology jargon: ideate, from 'idea', means to picture or conceive something in the mind.

entries.clue: Appreciative, having plenty of petrol to cover start of holiday (8)

indicatorNotes.to cover: TANKFUL covers H, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.start of: take the first letter of holiday

annotation.surface: A driver grateful to have enough fuel for the start of a trip.
annotation.walkthrough: Petrol is the British word for gasoline.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to appreciate a kindness is to be full of thanks for it.

entries.clue: Sheet of paper primarily focusing on a type of stew (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letter of focusing
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, F sits on top of OLIO

blocks.note: an olio is a spicy Spanish stew

annotation.surface: A page given over mainly to one particular stew recipe.
annotation.walkthrough: Olio, a stew and also a hotchpotch, is a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A printing term: a folio is a leaf, a sheet folded once, which also gives its name to the large folio book size.

entries.clue: Wrapped son’s injuries (6)

annotation.surface: A son's injuries being bandaged.
annotation.walkthrough: WOUND as in winding a bandage is said differently from the WOUNDS of the answer, which is the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a wound is an injury where the skin is cut or broken, the kind a bandage is wrapped round.

entries.clue: Bishop involved in test of ethnic group (6)

indicatorNotes.involved in: B is caught up inside TRIAL

blocks.note: b = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A bishop taking part in a study of an ethnic community.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of ethnic group' means relating to a tribe.
annotation.definitionFit: Tribal means belonging to a tribe, an ethnic group.

entries.clue: Run past when speaking (3)

indicatorNotes.when speaking: the word for past is said out loud

annotation.surface: An instruction to jog past someone mid-conversation.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched; 'Run' looks like a verb but is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A bye is a run credited without the batsman hitting the ball.

entries.clue: Critical remark from chap cutting opening of bridge club (8)

indicatorNotes.cutting: RICK cuts in between B and BAT
indicatorNotes.opening of: take the first letter of bridge

annotation.surface: A man slicing the ribbon to open a bridge club makes a barbed comment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bridge club' reads as a card club; the two words split apart.
annotation.definitionFit: A brickbat, literally a thrown bit of brick, is a harsh criticism.

entries.clue: Fellow with jewel, but wanting Liberal leadership (8)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so GEM comes along right after HE
indicatorNotes.wanting: 'wanting' means lacking, so ONLY goes without its L

blocks.note: but = only; remove L for Liberal

annotation.surface: A man with a gem who lacks the leadership of the Liberals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'But' is ONLY, as in 'but a child'; the surface makes 'Liberal leadership' one phrase, but 'leadership' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Hegemony is leadership or dominance, especially of one state over others.

entries.clue: English archdeacon following the Spanish team (6)

indicatorNotes.following: to follow is to come behind, so the English archdeacon, E VEN, comes after EL

annotation.surface: An English clergyman trailing the Spanish side.
annotation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, shortened to Ven.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team has eleven players and is called an eleven.
